## Applied Exercises

Work on these exercises in a copy of Charles River Reports.pbix, saved with **File > Save as** after you finish this chapter's tutorials, such as `Ch14 Exercises.pbix`. Build each exercise on its own report page, or in its own query tab in DAX query view, named after it (such as `Ex 14.1`), and put the measures it asks for in a display folder of the Key Measures table with the same name. Do not change the queries, relationships, measures, or pages the tutorials created, except where an exercise tells you to change something temporarily and undo it. When an exercise needs a Table the tutorials did not load, import it under the query name the exercise gives.

### Financial Accounting Exercises

**Exercise 14.1: The Balance Sheet at Any Month-End**

**Table group:** Accounting Core

**Scenario.** The controller wants a balance sheet beside the income statement of Tutorial 14.3, at the end of whichever month the reader selects and before that year's closing entries, so that it can be compared with the pre-closing balance sheet of Chapter 6.

**Requirements.**

(1) Add the measure below. A balance is cumulative, so the measure removes the filters on the Date table and keeps every posting up to the last day in the filter context. Explain in one sentence each what its three filter arguments do, and why the closing entries are left out only when they are posted on that day.

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Balance =
VAR AsOf = MAX ( 'Date'[Date] )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        SUM ( GLEntry[Debit] ) - SUM ( GLEntry[Credit] ),
        REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Date' ),
        'Date'[Date] <= AsOf,
        NOT ( GLEntry[IsYearEndClose] && GLEntry[PostingDate] = AsOf )
    )
```

(2) Build a matrix with AccountType and AccountSubType from Account on **Rows** and Balance as **Values**, and a slicer with YearMonth set to single selection. Select 2026-12 and confirm three things: the total of the matrix is zero; the assets equal the liabilities, the equity, and the balance of the revenue and expense accounts, each with its sign reversed; and that last balance equals the net income of fiscal 2026 from Tutorial 14.3.

(3) Select 2026-06, and then 2024-12. Confirm that the matrix still totals zero in both, and explain why the revenue and expense accounts at June 2026 hold only six months of postings, although the ledger begins in January 2024.

(4) Write two variants of the measure: one with no filter on the closing entries, and one built on GL Amount, which leaves out all of them. At 2026-12, compare the equity and the revenue and expense balances of the three measures. Say which variant gives a post-closing balance sheet, and what is wrong with the other.

(5) In a table visual, list the accounts whose NormalBalance is the opposite of the usual side for their AccountType (debit for assets and expenses; credit for liabilities, equity, and revenue). Explain why a statement whose signs followed each account's NormalBalance would misstate its subtotals.

**Deliverable.** The page with the matrix, the two variant measures, and a short note answering requirements (1) and (3) to (5).

**Exercise 14.2: Revenue by Invoice Date and by Ship Date**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash

**Scenario.** Chapter 12's auditor found invoices posted in the year after the goods were delivered. The controller wants the report to show each year's revenue by invoice date beside its revenue by the date the goods shipped, and to list the invoice lines that cross from one year to the next.

**Requirements.**

(1) Import T14_Shipment as a query named `ShipmentHeaders`, keeping ShipmentID and ShipmentDate, and T15_ShipmentLine as `ShipmentLines`, keeping ShipmentLineID and ShipmentID. Clear **Enable load** on both.

(2) Import T17_SalesInvoiceLine again as `ShippedLines`, keeping SalesInvoiceLineID, SalesInvoiceID, ItemID, ShipmentLineID, and LineTotal. Merge it with SalesInvoice to bring InvoiceNumber and InvoiceDate, with ShipmentLines to bring ShipmentID, and then with ShipmentHeaders to bring ShipmentDate, each a left outer join expanded without the prefix. Set both dates to the **Date** type.

(3) Relate ShippedLines to Item on ItemID and to Date on InvoiceDate. Then drag ShipmentDate from ShippedLines onto Date in the Date table. Confirm that Power BI drew the second relationship as a dashed line, and explain why it cannot be active.

(4) Add the measure `Shipped Revenue = SUM ( ShippedLines[LineTotal] )` and the measure below, and build a matrix with Year from Date on **Rows** and both measures as **Values**. Confirm that Shipped Revenue equals the revenue of the Validation page in each year, and explain the row labeled (Blank).

<!-- dax-check: skip -->
```
Revenue by Ship Date =
CALCULATE (
    [Shipped Revenue],
    USERELATIONSHIP ( ShippedLines[ShipmentDate], 'Date'[Date] )
)
```

(5) Add a custom column named `CrossesYear` to ShippedLines, true when ShipmentDate is not null and its year differs from the year of InvoiceDate. List the lines for which it is true in a table visual with InvoiceNumber, InvoiceDate, ShipmentDate, and LineTotal. Sort them into two kinds, invoices issued after the year in which the goods shipped and invoices dated before their shipment, and compare each kind with Chapter 12's revenue cutoff findings.

(6) Recommend which date the monthly sales report should use for revenue, and what the report should disclose about the other.

**Deliverable.** The queries, the matrix and the table visual on the Ex 14.2 page, and a short note answering requirements (3) to (6).

### Managerial Accounting Exercises

**Exercise 14.3: Monthly Comparisons with the Prior Year**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Item table from Master Data

**Scenario.** The marketing manager wants each item group's revenue by month beside the same month of the year before, and the year to date beside the prior year to date, for fiscal 2026.

**Requirements.**

(1) Write the measures Revenue PY, with SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, and Revenue YoY %, the change against it with DIVIDE. Write Revenue YTD, with TOTALYTD, and Revenue PY YTD, which applies SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR to Revenue YTD, and YTD Change %.

(2) Build a matrix with ItemGroup on **Rows**, YearMonth on **Columns**, and Revenue YoY % as **Values**, filtered to 2026. Find Furniture's largest decline and largest increase against the prior year, and compare them with your results for Exercise 11.2, which took revenue from the ledger.

(3) For December 2026, compare Revenue YTD with Revenue PY YTD for each item group and in total. Which groups grew in fiscal 2026, and which shrank?

(4) Find the item group whose monthly comparisons swing the most. Add a measure that counts the invoice lines of the group in each month, and explain why a percentage change is a weak guide for that group.

(5) Build a table visual with Year, Revenue, and Revenue PY and no filter. Explain the row for 2027, and change Revenue PY so that it is blank wherever Revenue is blank.

**Deliverable.** The measures, the matrix and the table visual on the Ex 14.3 page, and a short note answering requirements (2) to (5).

**Exercise 14.4: The Furniture Bridge as Measures**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Item table from Master Data

**Scenario.** Chapter 6's bridge explained the fall in Furniture's margin for one pair of quarters, on a worksheet. The controller wants the bridge in the model, so that it can be read for any quarter and any item group.

**Requirements.**

(1) Add the measures `Units = SUM ( SalesInvoiceLine[Quantity] )` and `Margin PQ = CALCULATE ( [Gross Margin], DATEADD ( 'Date'[Date], -1, QUARTER ) )`. DATEADD shifts the dates in the filter context back one quarter.

(2) Add the volume effect below, which follows cell B17 of Tutorial 6.3: the change in units at the prior quarter's margin per unit. Then write Mix Effect, Price List Effect, and Promotion Effect in the same way, following B18 to B20. They use the list margin per unit, `([List Amount] - [Standard Cost]) / [Units]`, the price-list reduction per unit, `([List Amount] - [Revenue] - [Discounts]) / [Units]`, and the discount per unit, `[Discounts] / [Units]`, each in the current quarter and in the prior one.

<!-- dax-check: skip -->
```
Volume Effect =
VAR PriorQuarter = DATEADD ( 'Date'[Date], -1, QUARTER )
VAR UnitsPQ = CALCULATE ( [Units], PriorQuarter )
VAR MarginPerUnitPQ =
    CALCULATE ( DIVIDE ( [Gross Margin], [Units] ), PriorQuarter )
RETURN
    ( [Units] - UnitsPQ ) * MarginPerUnitPQ
```

(3) Add a Bridge Check measure equal to Margin PQ plus the four effects less Gross Margin. Explain why this model needs no cost effect.

(4) Build a matrix with YearQuarter on **Rows**, filtered to 2026 and to Furniture, and Margin PQ, the four effects, Gross Margin, and Bridge Check as **Values**. Confirm that the 2026-Q4 row reproduces Chapter 6's bridge and that Bridge Check is zero in every row.

(5) Read the 2026-Q3 row, the change from the second quarter. Which effects explain it, and how does it differ from the fourth quarter's?

(6) Change the item group filter to Lighting. Which effect explains most of Lighting's change in the fourth quarter of 2026?

**Deliverable.** The measures and the matrix on the Ex 14.4 page, and a short note answering requirements (3), (5), and (6).

### Auditing Exercises

**Exercise 14.5: Testing the Model's Relationships**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash and Accounting Core

**Scenario.** Before the report is shared, the internal auditor reviews the model the way Chapter 12 reviewed queries, by testing what each relationship does to the numbers. Rather than change the model, the auditor writes queries that change a relationship for one calculation with CROSSFILTER, a function that sets the cross filter direction of a relationship inside CALCULATE.

**Requirements.**

(1) In a DAX query view tab named `Ex 14.5`, run the query below. It counts customers three ways for each item group in fiscal 2026: the rows of the Customer table, the distinct customers of the invoice lines, and the rows of the Customer table with the relationship set to Both. Explain the three results, and say which count a report should use.

<!-- dax-check: query -->
```
// Customers by item group, fiscal 2026, counted three ways
DEFINE
    MEASURE Customer[Customer Rows] = COUNTROWS ( Customer )
    MEASURE Customer[Customers Invoiced] =
        DISTINCTCOUNT ( SalesInvoiceLine[CustomerID] )
    MEASURE Customer[Customer Rows Both] =
        CALCULATE (
            COUNTROWS ( Customer ),
            CROSSFILTER ( SalesInvoiceLine[CustomerID], Customer[CustomerID], BOTH )
        )
EVALUATE
SUMMARIZECOLUMNS (
    'Item'[ItemGroup],
    TREATAS ( { 2026 }, 'Date'[Year] ),
    "Customer Rows", [Customer Rows],
    "Customers Invoiced", [Customers Invoiced],
    "Customer Rows Both", [Customer Rows Both]
)
```

(2) Write a query that shows, for each item group in fiscal 2026, Operating Expense, Operating Expense with the relationship between SalesInvoiceLine[InvoiceDate] and Date set to Both, and the number of dates left in the Date table under the same setting. Explain what the Services row means, and how it illustrates the Watch out on two fact tables in this chapter's section on relationships.

(3) Write a query that shows, for each item group in fiscal 2026, the share of revenue calculated with `REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Item' )` and with `ALL ( SalesInvoiceLine )`. Add up each column of shares, and explain what each total is a share of.

(4) Write a short list of the relationship and filter settings you would look for when you review a model someone else built, with the test that reveals each.

**Deliverable.** The query tab and a memo answering requirements (1) to (4).

**Exercise 14.6: A Library of Control Totals**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash and Accounting Core

**Scenario.** The auditor wants one query that proves the model agrees with the control totals established in Parts II and III, can be run again after every change to the model, and reports a pass or a fail for each test.

**Requirements.**

(1) In a query tab named `Control Totals`, type the query below, which holds two tests, and replace each expected value of 0 with the control total you established in Chapter 6. Then add one ROW for each of these tests, with its expected value from the chapter given: the net income of fiscal 2026 (Tutorial 14.3), the debits of all journal entries in the ledger (Chapter 8), the manufacturing variance posted to account 5080 in fiscal 2026 without the closing entries (Chapter 10), and the revenue posted by sales invoices to accounts 4010 to 4040 and 4080 in fiscal 2026 (Exercise 10.1).

<!-- dax-check: query -->
```
// Control totals: each test must agree within one cent
EVALUATE
VAR Tests =
    UNION (
        ROW ( "Test", "Invoice lines, fiscal 2026", "Expected", 0,
            "Actual", CALCULATE ( [Invoice Lines], 'Date'[Year] = 2026 ) ),
        ROW ( "Test", "Revenue, fiscal 2026", "Expected", 0,
            "Actual", CALCULATE ( [Revenue], 'Date'[Year] = 2026 ) )
    )
RETURN
    ADDCOLUMNS (
        Tests,
        "Difference", ROUND ( [Actual] - [Expected], 2 ),
        "Result", IF ( ABS ( [Actual] - [Expected] ) <= 0.01, "Pass", "Fail" )
    )
```

(2) Run the query. The revenue posted by sales invoices differs from the revenue of the invoice lines. Explain the difference, and add a test that the difference equals its documented cause.

(3) In your exercise copy, change GL Amount so that it no longer leaves out the closing entries, run the tests again, and record which fail and which do not. Then undo the change and run them once more.

(4) Write a conclusion of a few sentences: what the passing tests show about the model, what they cannot show, and when the library should be run.

**Deliverable.** The Control Totals tab and the conclusion.
